claims.claim: ice-out advanced 1.8 days per decade over the 50 years to 2008 but 0.4–0.6 over 75–125 years (abstract)
claims.note: abstract only. The abstract (USGS record) gives 1.8 days/decade for the last 50 years (median of lakes with adequate data), 0.6 for 75 years, 0.4 for 100 and 0.6 for 125 years, periods ending in 2008, 28 New England lakes — consistent with the paper's sentence, which already says 'abstract'.

claims.claim: at three New England lakes earlier ice-out brought lower late-summer bottom oxygen, explaining 32–46 % of its variation (abstract)
claims.note: abstract only. The abstract: 'Based on historical data available at three lakes, 32 to 46 % of the interannual variability of late summer hypolimnion DO levels was related to ice-out dates; earlier ice-outs were associated with lower DO levels.' Consistent with the paper.
